title: UX Tips for Multi-Step Forms
summary: This lesson teaches how to optimize long forms by converting them into multi-step wizards. It highlights key techniques like chunking, progress visualization, contextual grouping, and inline validation to reduce cognitive load and improve completion rates.

transcript.text: Twelve fields, one wall. Four steps, one path.
The brain reads three fields without effort. Twelve in a row, trigger scroll fatigue.
Chunking lowers cognitive load before it kills it.
Progress shows where you are. Linear bar, numbered dots, step labels. Pick one.
Users need to feel the end is close.
Group fields by context, not by count. Personal, shipping, payment, review.
Each step earns its own screen. Random splits feel arbitrary and slow.
Validate inside the step, not at the end.
Wrong email on step one shouldn't surface on step four.
Block next when invalid. Inline red beats final-screen rejection.
Save state on every step change. Back button preserves data. Refresh too.
Lose the form once, you lose the user forever.
Follow for more UX systems. Save this for your next signup flow.

on_screen_text: INLINE - INSTANT vs FINAL - TOO LATE
before_after: A single-page form with 12 fields (the 'Wall') is transformed into a 4-step wizard (the 'Path') that uses chunking and progress tracking.
